title: The zero-coefficient section of universal incidence
statement: Let f:Y -> Spec k be a scheme over a field, L an invertible module, and s_i a finite family of global sections. There exists a morphism z:Y -> H to the universal incidence scheme of [def-zl-bertini-universal-family] whose composite with the natural projection H -> Y is the identity. It is constructed by setting every coefficient parameter to zero. Scheme conventions, invertible modules and zero schemes use [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-sc-invertible-module] and [def-pc-zero-scheme]. The variable type may be empty and Y need not be reduced or nonempty.

source.place: Situation 0G47, situation-family-divisors, universal divisor and its fibres

proof.text: The evaluation of the coefficient polynomial ring at zero and the identity of Y give a map to the ambient product by its pullback property. Pulling back the universal ideal gives the zero ideal by the proved universal base-change formula: every coefficient function is zero, so the section is zero. The closed-immersion lifting property therefore factors this map through H. Its composite with the second ambient projection is the identity by the pullback equations.

theorem exists_bertiniUniversalZeroSection
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (L : Y.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    {I : Type u} [Fintype I] (s : I → Γ(L, ⊤)) :
    ∃ z : Y ⟶ (bertiniUniversalIdeal f L s).subscheme,
      z ≫ (bertiniUniversalIdeal f L s).subschemeι ≫
        pullback.snd (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (MvPolynomial.C : k →+* MvPolynomial I k))) f = 𝟙 Y
